overview: Today's news is dominated by a sharp Delhi smog crisis after Diwali, a fresh spy allegation against Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang, a cautious but ongoing US-Iran negotiation, and the opening of the UN climate summit COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.

items.headline: Delhi's air turns severe after Diwali fireworks
items.summary: Air quality in Delhi worsened sharply on the day after Diwali, with a thick smog and readings close to the 'severe' category. Fireworks were set off despite a ban.
items.detail: Reports say revellers continued to burst illegal fireworks through Diwali, pushing the city's air quality toward the severe band on Monday. The BJP has blamed decades of inaction by previous administrations, while opposition parties have questioned the government's air quality data and raised the issue of the central government's responsibility. Delhi regularly sees winter smog driven by stubble burning in neighbouring states, vehicle emissions and dust, and Diwali firecrackers add a short, intense spike on top of that. Reports from Punjab also flagged a sharp single-day rise in farm fires on Diwali.
items.analysis: Watch whether the Supreme Court and state authorities move quickly on enforcement, since the court has already sought action plans on vehicular pollution from Delhi and three states.

items.headline: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang at the centre of a Chinese spy probe
items.summary: A Chinese-linked executive named Alice Huang has been accused of spying on Nvidia, and Jensen Huang has publicly acknowledged a past personal affair with someone described as a suspected spy. China has rejected the spying charge as baseless.
items.detail: Reports say Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a person described as a suspected Chinese spy, while discussing the broader scandal in which Alice Huang is the executive accused. Nvidia's board has issued a formal statement on the matter. China's government has denied the allegations, calling them a smear. The case lands at a sensitive time for the US-China technology rivalry, because Nvidia's advanced AI chips are central to export controls and to the competition over AI.
items.analysis: The story matters for investors and policymakers alike, because it links a company at the heart of the AI chip market to national security concerns; the board's response and any official findings will be closely watched.

items.headline: Trump says renewed strikes on Iran are highly unlikely while talks continue
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said fresh US strikes on Iran are highly unlikely as nuclear negotiations continue, though he has not ruled them out. US and Iranian officials are reportedly negotiating quietly.
items.detail: Trump has said he is unlikely to order new strikes if talks progress, while warning that he could still act. Reports describe the US and Iran as quietly negotiating as the wider Middle East remains on edge. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has played down the chances of a quick breakthrough. Gulf states, including the UAE, have said that a US-Iran settlement appears difficult, and the conflict has already affected shipping, oil prices and air travel in the region.
items.analysis: Whether talks hold will shape oil prices, Gulf flight schedules and the risk of further attacks on infrastructure in the region.

items.headline: US and Iran negotiate as the Middle East stays on edge
items.summary: Washington and Tehran are discussing Iran's nuclear programme through quiet channels, but no breakthrough has been announced. Rubio has tempered expectations.
items.detail: The talks follow a period of military confrontation between the US, Israel and Iran, which has disrupted Gulf airspace and shipping. Trump has said new strikes are unlikely if negotiations keep moving, but has kept the option open. Rubio has said chances of a major breakthrough are limited for now. Separately, the US has launched a task force aimed at disrupting Iran's land transit routes, and Rubio is due to discuss Iran, Ukraine and AI with G7 allies in France.
items.analysis: The key question is whether a framework emerges that reduces strikes without a comprehensive nuclear deal, which would still leave many issues unresolved.

items.headline: Trump says immigration crackdown was too tough after midterm setback
items.summary: In a 60 Minutes interview, Trump said his immigration policy was 'too tough' and that it played a part in Republican losses in the US midterm elections.
items.detail: Trump's comments mark a shift in tone on deportation policy, and reports say he floated an amnesty-style arrangement in the interview. The Republican defeat in the midterms has triggered debate within the party, including over corruption claims and the role of key advisers. Commentators are split on whether the result signals a wider change in the political mood or a short-term reaction to specific issues.
items.analysis: Watch whether the White House turns these remarks into concrete policy or whether they remain a signal ahead of the next election cycle.

items.headline: Democrats push to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth after midterm wins
items.summary: Democrats, buoyed by their midterm gains, say they will push for impeachment of Pete Hegseth and launch probes of Trump allies. Some Republicans have also turned critical of him.
items.detail: House Democrats have said they are a hard yes on impeachment, and the party's leadership has backed the move. Reports also say some Republicans have distanced themselves from Hegseth following the midterm losses. Impeachment in the US House requires a simple majority, but conviction would need two-thirds of the Senate, which makes removal unlikely. The debate is partly about the administration's handling of military matters and the broader Iran conflict.
items.analysis: The push is a sign of how the new House majority may shape oversight of the executive over the next two years.

items.headline: Trump to meet Putin and Xi next week
items.summary: Trump is set to hold meetings with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping in the coming week, according to reports.
items.detail: The planned meetings come as the US is seeking to manage several crises at once, including the Iran conflict and the war in Ukraine. Separately, talks involving the US, Europe and Russia on Ukraine are set to take place in Abu Dhabi, where Europeans have said they will join. Reports also note that China has extended a suspension of an additional 24 per cent tariff on US goods for two months while retaining a 10 per cent levy.
items.analysis: Trade and security issues are likely to be linked, so the outcome of these meetings could affect tariffs, Ukraine and Middle East diplomacy together.

items.headline: Pope Leo criticises Argentina's austerity measures during visit
items.summary: Pope Leo delivered a pointed rebuke of President Javier Milei's austerity policies during his visit to Argentina, as part of a wider Latin American trip.
items.detail: Reports describe the Pope's remarks as stinging, with the Church drawing attention to the social cost of spending cuts. Milei's government has argued that tight fiscal policy is needed to tame long-running inflation and debt in Argentina. The Pope's trip also includes Peru and other stops in South America, and commentators have described it as one with a strong political dimension.
items.analysis: The visit highlights the Catholic Church's continuing role as a voice on economic inequality in Latin America.

items.headline: Train collision in Egypt kills at least seven
items.summary: Two trains collided near Cairo, killing at least seven people and injuring dozens more, according to reports.
items.detail: Reports describe a passenger train derailing after hitting another train in the Giza area near Cairo. Figures vary between outlets, with some reporting higher numbers of injured people. Egypt has a long history of rail accidents linked to ageing infrastructure, and rail safety has been a recurring public concern in the country.
items.analysis: Investigators will need to establish whether signalling, maintenance or human error was responsible, and whether any changes follow.

items.headline: Kharge's 'Eid of happiness' remark on Diwali sparks political row
items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge described Diwali as an 'Eid of happiness' in his greetings, prompting the BJP and allies to accuse him of appeasement.
items.detail: BJP spokespersons said the remark was a twisted message that hurt Hindu sentiments, and dared Congress to describe Eid as 'Diwali of joy'. Other BJP leaders, including Bihar BJP chief Sanjay Saraogi, criticised the remark, and the Shiv Sena also hit back. Congress has not been quoted in these reports responding in detail, and the row reflects a wider pattern of festival greetings being debated as political messaging ahead of upcoming state contests.
items.analysis: Such exchanges often shape the tone of campaigns in the run-up to state elections, even when they have little direct policy content.

items.headline: Parliament's Monsoon session stays formally open for a record 88 days
items.summary: Parliament's Monsoon session has remained unprorogued for 88 days, a record. Amit Shah has offered a special session on the SIR voter-roll revision issue, after Rahul Gandhi challenged PM Modi to an open debate.
items.detail: Reports say the session has not been formally ended since August, breaking a 2008 record for the longest such gap. Home Minister Amit Shah has offered a special session to discuss the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, after Rahul Gandhi challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an open debate. The government says the SIR is needed to keep voter lists accurate, while the opposition argues it risks removing eligible voters and wants fuller scrutiny.
items.analysis: Whether the special session goes ahead, and how the government and opposition frame it, may shape the winter session agenda.

items.headline: Opposition steps up attack on Election Commission over SIR and delimitation
items.summary: Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi has listed 10 alleged poll irregularities and linked the SIR, delimitation and EVMs in a 'Modi-Shah-ECI package'. The Election Commission has filed an affidavit rejecting such claims.
items.detail: Gogoi has targeted the Centre and the Election Commission on the SIR voter-roll process and on delimitation, which is the redrawing of constituency boundaries. The Election Commission's affidavit, which reports say was backed by all three commissioners, rejects the vote-theft charges as baseless. The INDIA bloc has announced a second phase of its campaign against the Chief Election Commissioner, including state-level protests and a push in the winter session. The Supreme Court has also sought responses on a law giving lifelong immunity to the CEC and Election Commissioners.
items.analysis: The dispute goes to the credibility of electoral institutions, so the Supreme Court's response to the immunity question will be closely followed.

items.headline: Assembly elections in five states likely to be announced in January
items.summary: Sources say elections for five state assemblies may be announced in January, according to News18.
items.detail: Reports cite unnamed sources, so the timing is not confirmed by the Election Commission. Electoral rolls remain at the centre of the national debate, with disputes in West Bengal over the validity of the state election and reports of roll discrepancies in Rajasthan. Parties are already positioning themselves on issues from voter lists to local campaigns.
items.analysis: Any announcement will be scrutinised in light of the ongoing SIR dispute and the Election Commission's handling of voter rolls.

items.headline: Row over Delhi's pollution as BJP and AAP trade blame
items.summary: The BJP has alleged a conspiracy over Delhi's pollution, while AAP and Congress have questioned the AQI data being published.
items.detail: Delhi's government and opposition parties have clashed over the smog that followed Diwali. The BJP has blamed years of policy inaction by previous governments, while opposition parties have asked whether the air quality data is accurate and who is responsible for enforcement. The debate is part of a longer political argument over how to control winter pollution in the capital.
items.analysis: Public confidence in air quality data is itself a political issue, so independent monitoring and transparent enforcement will matter as much as rhetoric.

items.headline: Keralam begins random petrol checks for excess ethanol after Karnataka findings
items.summary: Keralam has started random testing of petrol at select fuel outlets across four districts after Karnataka reported high ethanol levels in samples.
items.detail: Karnataka's Chief Minister said the state had tested petrol samples at 67 locations over complaints about ethanol blending. Keralam then launched inspections and sample testing at pumps, with the Union Minister Suresh Gopi saying the state is free to test and warning against politicising the issue. He has defended the government's E20 fuel policy, which blends petrol with 20 per cent ethanol. The checks are meant to confirm whether blending levels are within the prescribed limits.
items.analysis: The results will matter for vehicle owners and fuel companies, and could bring clearer rules on E20 blending.

items.headline: Court denies regular bail to actors in Kochi doctor assault case
items.summary: A Kerala court has denied regular bail to actors Athulya Chandra and Bipin Perumpally in a doctor assault case, two days after their arrest.
items.detail: Reports say the court refused regular bail, so the two remain in custody while the case proceeds. The case involves an alleged assault on a doctor in Kochi. Under Indian procedure, the accused can apply again for bail or approach a higher court, and the investigation will continue to determine the charges.
items.analysis: The case has drawn attention to safety for medical staff, and the bail process will be watched closely.

items.headline: Keralam mulls permanent disqualification of licences for drunk driving
items.summary: The state is considering permanently disqualifying driving licences for drunk driving, according to reports.
items.detail: The proposal is at an early stage and is being discussed as a tougher deterrent against drink-driving. Separately, the Chief Minister has said strict action will be taken against reckless driving by private buses. Kozhikode police have also registered cases against vehicle owners for underage driving, reflecting a wider push on road safety.
items.analysis: Any change would need legal review under the Motor Vehicles Act, so details on how permanent disqualification would work will be important.

items.headline: Report says Kerala government kept Cellebrite phone-unlocking software
items.summary: A report says Kerala's previous CPI(M)-led government bought phone-unlocking software from Israeli firm Cellebrite in 2024, and the current Congress-led government renewed it in July.
items.detail: The report, carried by Maktoob, says the software is used to access data from locked phones, a tool widely used by police and investigators. Privacy and civil liberties groups often raise concerns about such tools, and the report does not in these headlines describe any misuse. The issue crosses party lines, since both the previous and current governments are involved in the purchase and renewal.
items.analysis: The debate touches on the balance between police investigative powers and digital privacy, an issue likely to continue in the state assembly.

items.headline: Great Nicobar airport land acquisition declaration deadline extended by one year
items.summary: The Andaman and Nicobar Administration has extended by one year the statutory period for making the declaration on land acquisition for the Great Nicobar airport.
items.detail: According to local reporting, the extension applies to the declaration step under land acquisition law, which allows the administration to move forward with formal acquisition. The Great Nicobar project, which includes an airport and port infrastructure, has long been contested over its environmental impact on forests and the indigenous Shompen and Nicobarese communities. The extension gives the administration more time, but the project's clearances and tribal rights issues remain part of the wider debate.
items.analysis: Watch for court challenges or new environmental and tribal consultation steps, since these have shaped the project's pace so far.

items.headline: Low-pressure area over the Andaman Sea intensifies into a depression
items.summary: A low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal and near the Andaman and Nicobar Islands has intensified into a depression, according to Myanmar's meteorological department.
items.detail: A fresh low-pressure system over the Andaman Sea was also flagged by India's weather forecasters, who predicted it could strengthen into a depression within 48 hours. Such systems are common in this season and can bring heavy rain to the islands and coastal areas. Residents and shipping operators are typically advised to follow official warnings as conditions evolve.
items.analysis: The track and strength of the system will determine whether it affects the islands directly or passes further away.

items.headline: COP31 climate summit opens in Antalya amid extreme heat warnings
items.summary: The UN climate summit COP31 opened in Antalya, Türkiye, on Monday, running from 9 to 20 November, with planetary extremes described as off the charts.
items.detail: Reports say the summit opens as 2026 is shaping up as a record-hot year, with an El Niño event adding to global temperatures and October described as the warmest on record. India's Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav is preparing the country's climate diplomacy. Delegates are meeting against a backdrop of wars and geopolitical rivalry that are drawing attention away from climate commitments. COP negotiations are consensus-based and typically focus on emissions cuts, finance for vulnerable countries and adaptation.
items.analysis: The key test is whether countries agree on stronger finance and emissions measures despite the geopolitical tensions in the agenda.

items.headline: Proposed Western Ghats ecological protection zone stuck in notification delay
items.summary: The proposed ecological protection zone for the Western Ghats faces growing climate threats, but its formal notification remains pending.
items.detail: Reports say the zone would protect a sensitive mountain range that is home to rich biodiversity and that feeds many rivers. Climate-driven rainfall shifts and landslide risks are increasing pressure on the region. Debates over development and protection in the Western Ghats have run for years, with states and local communities often weighing protection against livelihoods.
items.analysis: Delays in notification leave the area with uncertain protection, and climate stress is making those decisions more urgent.

items.headline: LIC says IRDAI's proposed commission cuts will have limited impact
items.summary: Life Insurance Corporation of India says the regulator's proposed commission reforms will have limited impact on its business, while brokers have lobbied the government against the distribution changes.
items.detail: LIC has said its distribution network is largely ring-fenced from the proposed norms and that its expense ratio is lower than many peers. Reports say the company is seeking a calibrated rollout and has flagged agents' interests. Separately, brokers have met Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and officials in the Prime Minister's Office to ask for intervention against the proposals. The reforms aim to change how commissions are paid to insurance distributors, which is a long-running policy question in India.
items.analysis: Higher-cost insurers and smaller distributors may feel more pressure, so the final design of the rules will matter for the market structure.

items.headline: Medical tourism growth may depend on global health insurance cover
items.summary: Apollo Hospitals' Sangita Reddy says broader insurance access for international patients could help medical tourism in India grow.
items.detail: Reports say Apollo sees international cover as a way to attract more overseas patients to India. An Asia Insurance Review piece also argues that global health insurers can give a boost to medical tourism. For international private medical insurance (IPMI) providers, the trend could mean more cross-border treatment packages and more claims involving hospitals abroad.
items.analysis: Growth in cross-border care would also raise questions about claim processes, pricing and quality standards across borders.

items.headline: Aon creates a North American healthcare unit and RGA's premiums climb
items.summary: Broker Aon has set up a North American healthcare unit, while reinsurer RGA reported a 25 per cent rise in consolidated net premiums for the third quarter.
items.detail: Aon's new unit is led by Nick Gaudiosi and is designed to focus on the healthcare sector across North America. RGA, a major life and health reinsurer, reported net premiums of $5.4 billion for the third quarter of 2026, up 25 per cent. Reinsurers and brokers are increasingly building specialised units as healthcare costs and risk models become more complex.
items.analysis: Specialist healthcare units show where brokers and reinsurers see growth as medical costs rise.

items.headline: Court rules insurer cannot deny a health claim without medical evidence
items.summary: A court ruling reported this week says an insurer cannot reject a health claim without proper medical evidence, and a five-year rule protects policyholders from arbitrary rejection.
items.detail: Commentary on IRDAI's five-year rule explains that after a set period of continuous cover, insurers generally cannot reject a claim on the basis of non-disclosure, subject to the policy terms. The court decision reinforces the principle that denials must be backed by evidence. Consumers in India are advised by regulators to read the policy's moratorium clause carefully, as it sets out when claims are protected.
items.analysis: Such rulings tend to shape how insurers document and defend claim rejections, which is useful background for anyone following consumer protection in health cover.

items.headline: Drone attack injures four at Dubai Airport
items.summary: Four people were injured in a drone attack at Dubai Airport, which has been linked by reports to Iran's escalating operations in the Gulf.
items.detail: Reports say the incident is part of a broader pattern of attacks in the region that has affected airports and shipping routes. Earlier this week, an attempted missile attack damaged an Aramco building in Riyadh, and Saudi Arabia has reported intercepting missiles. Dubai's airport authorities have been publishing guidance for travellers, including rules on banned items and baggage.
items.analysis: Travellers should keep an eye on official airline and airport updates, as security conditions are changing quickly.

items.headline: Flight cancellations continue as airlines suspend Saudi routes until November 19
items.summary: UAE carriers have suspended flights to Saudi Arabia until 19 November, extending disruption caused by the regional conflict.
items.detail: Reports say flight schedules across the Gulf have been disrupted since the conflict escalated, and some Gulf carriers have been asked to shift flights to Navi Mumbai. Airline losses are also mounting, with one analysis projecting a large net loss for Middle Eastern airlines in 2026 because of airspace closures. Passengers are advised to check with their airline before travel.
items.analysis: The duration of these suspensions will depend largely on security developments and diplomacy with Iran.

items.headline: UAE trade grows double digits in the first nine months of 2026
items.summary: A senior official says UAE trade maintained double-digit growth in the first nine months of 2026, despite regional tensions.
items.detail: The figure comes from the Under-Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Trade, who spoke about the country's trade performance so far this year. Trade growth has been a central part of the UAE's economic strategy, supported by its ports, free zones and trade agreements. Regional conflicts and shipping disruptions have made logistics costs and insurance more of a concern for traders.
items.analysis: Sustained trade growth despite disruption suggests the UAE's logistics network is adapting, but risks remain if shipping routes stay unsettled.

items.headline: UAE weather: temperatures dip, with heavy rain possible in eastern and coastal areas
items.summary: Temperatures are forecast to dip on Tuesday, with heavy rain possible in parts of the eastern and coastal UAE.
items.detail: The national meteorological forecast points to some relief from the warmth, with rain more likely in the east and along the coast. Heavy rain can cause localised flooding and traffic disruption, especially on roads not built for sudden downpours. Residents should follow official weather alerts for the latest guidance.
items.analysis: Rain forecasts can change rapidly, so the latest official updates are the best guide for travel plans.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty slip as IT stocks drag and investors book profits
items.summary: Indian equities opened lower on Monday after a sharp rally, with IT shares weighing on the indices and Sensex falling about 94 points in early trade.
items.detail: Reports say profit-taking after the Diwali rally was a key factor, with the Nifty slipping below 25,000 and then toward 24,900 at points in the session. Losses were led by Nifty IT, Metal, FMCG and Oil & Gas, while pharma, PSU banks and private banks gave some support. The Sensex had closed only marginally lower in the special Muhurat trading session on the Diwali holiday, ending a seven-day rally.
items.analysis: Markets are sensitive to global tech moves, so swings in IT stocks often reflect sentiment about AI and US market developments.

items.headline: Rupee rises toward 93.7 against the dollar on foreign inflows and softer oil
items.summary: The rupee strengthened by around 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade, helped by foreign inflows and easing crude prices.
items.detail: Reports say the rupee has been on a winning streak, with foreign equity inflows and softer oil prices supporting it. Some reports note that the currency has reached a seven-month high. The Reserve Bank of India is also watched for its dollar-buying threshold, which is relevant when the rupee moves sharply in either direction.
items.analysis: Lower oil prices ease India's import bill, which is one reason the rupee has firmed, but geopolitical risks remain a swing factor.

items.headline: Gold rises on US-Iran peace hopes and a softer dollar
items.summary: Gold has climbed above $4,120 an ounce, helped by hopes of a US-Iran deal, a softer dollar and easing oil prices.
items.detail: Reports say lower oil prices have eased inflation worries, which tends to support gold as a store of value. Gold is also up around 4 per cent since the US midterm elections, according to one market report. Analysts are watching the US inflation data and the Federal Reserve's stance, since rate expectations affect the appeal of non-yielding assets like gold.
items.analysis: Gold tends to move with geopolitical risk and dollar expectations, so a breakdown in US-Iran talks could quickly change the picture.

items.headline: Global markets rally on tech gains and cooling oil, but Gift Nifty points to a firm start
items.summary: Asian and global equities recovered after an earlier tech rout, while the GIFT Nifty indicated a modestly positive open for India.
items.detail: Asian stock markets climbed after a tech sell-off, with Nvidia-related headlines and the AI sector in focus. The GIFT Nifty was trading around 25,018 in pre-open estimates, up about 38 points. Oil prices have eased, with Brent reported below $100 a barrel, and FPIs were reported to have invested over $4.1 billion recently. Markets also weigh US jobs data, which has raised expectations of a December rate hike.
items.analysis: The mix of AI-sector volatility, oil and US rate expectations is shaping near-term market direction.

items.headline: India launches three indigenous AI models
items.summary: India has launched three indigenous AI models, including a 26.3-billion-parameter model called EKA-1, according to a technology report.
items.detail: The report describes EKA-1 as a model with 26.3 billion parameters, along with offline-capable models in the Dhir series. Domestic AI models are seen as important for data sovereignty and for serving Indian languages and sectors. Such launches are often judged by how well they perform on local benchmarks and how widely they are adopted by government and industry.
items.analysis: The value of these models will depend on performance, openness and whether they find real users in public services and enterprises.

items.headline: Apple says 100,000 apps are already built for the iPhone Duo
items.summary: Apple says more than 100,000 apps have already been optimised for its iPhone Duo, a new device format.
items.detail: Apple has said developers have built or optimised a large number of apps for the device ahead of its wider availability. Reviewers have compared the device with Android foldables. A large developer base at launch is important for any new hardware, since app availability often decides whether a new form factor succeeds.
items.analysis: Developer support is a key early indicator, though long-term usage will depend on how well the apps take advantage of the new screen format.

items.headline: Reports say a Senate bill could fast-track AI data centre expansion
items.summary: A bipartisan Senate bill reportedly aims to fast-track the expansion of AI data centres, a development that unsettled IT stocks in India.
items.detail: The report says the proposal could speed up permits and infrastructure for AI data centres in the US. Expansion of data centres raises demand for chips, power and cooling, which benefits chipmakers and infrastructure firms but can also add pressure on electricity grids. The bill's progress and details will determine how much it affects investment plans.
items.analysis: AI infrastructure policy in the US has direct effects on global chip and cloud supply chains, including those serving Indian IT firms.

items.headline: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees
items.summary: Microsoft has offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees, prompting staff to publish an open letter raising concerns about the company's AI strategy.
items.detail: Reports say the buyout offer is part of a wider restructuring, with some employees questioning the direction of the company's AI plans. Chief executive Satya Nadella has reportedly spoken about a vision involving millions of AI agents. Large-scale buyouts are a common tool for reshaping workforces, and they often raise questions about job security across the tech sector.
items.analysis: The move reflects how big tech is balancing heavy AI spending with cost control and workforce planning.

items.headline: ISRO's GSLV-F18 mission carries NVS-03 navigation satellite
items.summary: ISRO has announced the GSLV-F18 mission carrying the NVS-03 navigation satellite, according to an official release.
items.detail: The GSLV is one of India's larger launch vehicles, and NVS-series satellites form part of the NavIC regional navigation system. NavIC provides positioning services across India and the surrounding region, and is used in areas such as transport, mapping and disaster management. Official releases describe these missions as steps in building India's space capabilities.
items.analysis: A successful launch would strengthen NavIC's constellation, which matters for independent positioning services.

items.headline: Carbon catalysts push solar water splitting toward cleaner hydrogen
items.summary: Researchers report that carbon-based catalysts can help drive solar water splitting, a route to making clean hydrogen from water and sunlight.
items.detail: Water splitting uses electricity or light to break water into hydrogen and oxygen, and the hydrogen can be used as a fuel without carbon emissions. The main challenge is finding catalysts that are cheap, durable and efficient. Carbon-based materials are attractive because they can be made from abundant elements, though long-term stability under real sunlight remains a hurdle.
items.analysis: The field is moving toward cheaper catalysts, but the question is whether efficiency and durability hold up outside the lab.

items.headline: Hydrogen storage tests in converted salt caverns
items.summary: EWE has completed a leak test at a salt-cavern hydrogen storage facility converted from natural gas use.
items.detail: Salt caverns are underground formations that can be sealed and used to store large volumes of gas. Converting them for hydrogen can offer large-scale, long-duration storage, which is important for balancing renewable power. Leak testing is a key step, since hydrogen molecules are very small and can escape through tiny gaps.
items.analysis: Passing a leak test is an important milestone, but commercial viability will depend on cost, safety and the pace of hydrogen demand.

items.headline: Nitrogen impurities found to poison catalysts in waste plastic pyrolysis oil
items.summary: Researchers have identified nitrogen-based impurities as a major cause of catalyst poisoning in oil produced from waste plastic pyrolysis.
items.detail: Pyrolysis heats waste plastic without oxygen to produce oil that can be refined into fuels or chemicals. Impurities in that oil can deactivate catalysts used in later upgrading steps, which slows down recycling. Reports say AI tools helped pinpoint the culprits, making the findings useful for designing better purification steps.
items.analysis: Understanding feedstock impurities is a practical bottleneck for plastic-to-fuel plants, so these findings may guide process design.

items.headline: arXiv: attaching honest error bars to machine-learned atomic potentials
items.summary: A new arXiv paper proposes a way to give calibrated uncertainty estimates for linear machine-learned interatomic potentials, tested on silicon.
items.detail: In plain terms, machine-learned potentials are fast stand-ins for quantum calculations of how atoms push and pull on each other. The authors argue that standard Bayesian error bars can be too small, because the models are imperfect in ways the statistics do not capture. Their approach uses a 'leave-one-out' resampling method, called a jackknife, to produce more honest error estimates for forces and material properties.
items.analysis: Reliable error bars help researchers know when a fast simulation can be trusted, which matters for materials design and battery or catalyst modelling.

items.headline: arXiv: designing superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
items.summary: A new arXiv preprint describes a method that lets a pretrained atomic foundation model be used in a differentiable way to search for crystals with target properties.
items.detail: Materials design usually means trying many candidate compositions and structures, which is slow. The authors' method, called DEFEAT, uses gradients to adjust both the elements and the atomic structure in a single optimisation. This is a step toward inverse design, where a researcher specifies a desired property and the computer proposes candidate materials, though it still needs experimental checks.
items.analysis: Inverse design could speed up discovery of new energy materials, but predictions from such models still require careful validation in the lab.

items.headline: Streetlights reduce crime, but the effect may not last
items.summary: A study finds that streetlights reduce crime, but the benefit does not seem to persist over the long term.
items.detail: The research suggests that improved lighting can deter crime in the short run, which is one reason cities invest in it. However, the effect appears to fade over time, which points to the importance of combining lighting with other measures. Urban planners often weigh such findings when deciding how to spend on public safety.
items.analysis: The finding suggests lighting is part of a broader safety toolkit rather than a permanent fix.

items.headline: Ancient Peruvian societies stayed largely peaceful despite sacrifices after El Niño floods
items.summary: Archaeologists report that ancient societies on Peru's northern desert coast were generally peaceful, even though they carried out ritual sacrifices after catastrophic El Niño flooding.
items.detail: Researchers studying how societies respond to extreme climate events found that mass ritual sacrifices along the northern Peruvian coast were linked to devastating flood events. Despite these drastic rituals, the wider societies appear to have been generally peaceful. The study offers a long-view perspective on how communities cope with climate shocks, which is relevant as El Niño returns this year.
items.analysis: Past responses to climate extremes offer context for today's debate on how societies adapt to rising climate risk.

items.headline: Scientists discover a new Amazon fish with a tiny natural range
items.summary: Researchers have described a new Amazon fish species found in pools in Brazil, with a range of only about 25 square kilometres, which may already be endangered.
items.detail: The species, named Laimosemion laranja, was found in small, threatened pools in Brazil. A very small natural range makes a species vulnerable to habitat loss, drought or pollution, even before it is formally assessed. Discoveries like this also highlight how much freshwater biodiversity in the Amazon remains poorly documented.
